singleTakeaway: Lucius can sound human enough to be mistaken for a teammate, and the conversation never needs a human handoff.
hook: Two half-screen phone frames are already live when the right-side message begins typing.

screens.purpose: Establish the dual-device premise and make the support conversation feel live.
screens.uiSurface: full-bleed Lucius stage with two half-screen phones already in frame
screens.layoutSnapshot: Left phone is Lucius and right phone is the user, both cropped by the frame edges and angled toward center while the right composer is active.
screens.background: Warm Ivory field with restrained Lucius atmosphere and subtle depth.
screens.primaryMotion: The right-side message types and sends.
screens.copyHint: Also, your product is really good. Why did you build it?

screens.purpose: Let Lucius's answer land as a natural, human-feeling response.
screens.uiSurface: same dual-phone stage with focus shifted slightly toward the Lucius device
screens.layoutSnapshot: The user message sits in the right phone history while the left phone composer shows a thinking state before the Lucius reply appears.
screens.background: Same stage, slightly calmer on the user side.
screens.primaryMotion: The Lucius answer generates into view.
screens.copyHint: Haha, thank you. We kept seeing the same support questions, so we built the product we wished we'd had.

screens.purpose: Show the user assuming Lucius is a real support person.
screens.uiSurface: same dual-phone stage with right phone reactivated
screens.layoutSnapshot: The left phone holds Lucius's answer while the right phone composer becomes active and sends a praise-driven follow-up.
screens.primaryMotion: The user praise message types and sends.
screens.copyHint: You've been incredibly helpful. What's your name? I want to tell your team.

screens.purpose: Deliver the reveal without breaking the conversational tone.
screens.uiSurface: same dual-phone stage with left device now clearly leading
screens.layoutSnapshot: The right-side praise sits visible while the left phone composer pauses and then resolves into a reveal reply.
screens.background: Same stage with a subtle Lucius emphasis strengthening on the left.
screens.copyHint: I'm Lucius, actually. Not a human agent, but thank you.

screens.purpose: Let the user react while the no-handoff proof resolves through motion.
screens.uiSurface: same dual-phone stage transitioning into a left-led composition
screens.layoutSnapshot: The right composer shifts from Thinking... to Wow. while the right phone is squeezed outward and a compact proof chip appears between the two devices.
screens.background: Same stage with motion focused through the center seam.
screens.primaryMotion: The right phone exits as the left phone takes center and the proof chip lands.

screens.purpose: Resolve the animation into Lucius branding without turning into a page.
screens.uiSurface: centered Lucius device dissolving into the Lucius mark and wordmark
screens.layoutSnapshot: The left device now owns the frame and zooms forward while the final proof sentence rises in below the mark.
screens.background: Same field stripped back to the calmest brand state.
screens.primaryMotion: The centered Lucius device resolves into the Lucius logo.
screens.copyHint: Support that feels human. No handoff required.

colorRoles: Use Warm Ivory as the field and Lucius Purple as the Lucius anchor.
Use Lavender Mist and Orchid Bloom only as restrained atmosphere.
Keep the user phone slightly cooler and more neutral than the Lucius phone.
typeRoles: Use SF Pro for all chat and state text.
Use Recoleta only in the final proof sentence.
Avoid oversized poster type during the dialogue screens.
radiusRules: Both devices should use coherent rounded hardware language.
Message bubbles and proof chips should share one soft-corner system.
backgroundRules: Use one full-bleed Lucius stage only.
Do not introduce page modules or dashboard framing.
graphicLanguage: Use device choreography instead of page composition.
Keep the phones as the only major compositional objects.
motionTone: Motion should feel cinematic, restrained, and readable.
The squeeze transition should feel spatial, not flashy.

nonGoals: Do not rebuild a literal Lucius product page.
Do not let the phones flatten into static poster cards.
Do not replace the reveal with a metric-only ending.
Do not add any extra proof points beyond the reveal and no-handoff close.
